newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate up on peso covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate up on peso covering.

text.p: * Done rates range from 11.375 to 11.0625 percent
Philippine interbank call loan rates edged up slightly to an average of 11.125 percent on Thursday from 11.09375 as some banks covered their short peso positions, traders said.

"This was the impact of the Central bank's dollar sales," a trader from a large commercial bank said. The Bank's dollar sales last Tuesday had an effect on banks' peso positions on Wednesday, which they cover only on the following day.
Though the Central Bank started buying dollars on Wednesday which would add peso liquidity to banks, "this was not yet enough," said a dealer.
Market volume rose to 21.438 billion pesos from 19.787 billion pesos. Out of the 51 participating financial institutions, 31 were lenders.
Meanwhile, T-bill trading at the secondary market saw offer rates being raised so banks could book trading profits and generate peso liquidity to ease their overnight positions, traders said.
The offer rate for the three-month bill was lifted to 11.60 percent from 11.50; the six-month bill to 11.925 from 11.70; and the one-year bill to 12.60 from 12.65, traders said.
